answer: Each agent must earn influence through a unique, slowly accumulated reputation tied to an anchor such as a scarce, nontransferable stake and verified task history. New accounts begin with negligible weight; splitting one identity into many does not multiply voting power, because each account must independently lock resources and build reliable performance. An attacker can forge names cheaply, but cannot cheaply forge years of useful work: sybils consume capital, time, and opportunities, while honest agents’ established records remain the umber line of trust.
